all_candidates.method: Signature kernel (untruncated, Goursat-PDE) + kernel-SVM/KRR on the 7-pair NY-session price PATH — cross-sectional direction
all_candidates.what: Replace truncated Lévy-area FEATURES with the full untruncated signature KERNEL k_sig(X,Y) computed as the solution of a Goursat PDE (sigkernel lib, KeOps-GPU). The signature kernel is reparametrization-invariant, order-sensitive, and provably more expressive than any fixed-depth truncation; it ranks top-2 vs all TSC baselines. Feed it to a kernel-SVM (sign) and kernel-ridge (rank) to classify the forward sign of the cross-sectional USD move.
all_candidates.novelty: Prior repo work (m30_sig.py, EXP116, SWEEP B7) used ONLY the truncated level-2 antisymmetric part (Lévy area) as tabular features into LightGBM, single-pair, and it was null at 30m/5m. The untruncated signature KERNEL is a categorically different object (infinite-depth, kernel-trick, no manual truncation/channel-pair selection) and was NEVER tried. Crucially it is applied to the multi-channel CROSS-PAIR path, where the only certified direction edge lives — signatures were only ever tried single-pair.
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (the 5.3M-row store) — close/log-return of all 7 USD pairs; NY-session flag from 239-feat store.
all_candidates.input_transform: Build the lifted path X_t = (t_norm, r_EURUSD, r_GBPUSD, ..., r_USDCAD) where r are 1m log-returns standardized per-pair (stationary). Take trailing windows of L=15-30 bars ENDING at each NY-session decision time (purge=1 horizon). Add time-augmentation (monotone t channel) and a basepoint (lead with 0) per the standard recipe so the kernel captures duration+translation. Each window is one path of dim d=8 (1 time + 7 returns), length L. Train sigkernel-SVM on train windows, label = sign of next-horizon EURUSD (or the USD-common-factor) move. CPCV-purge the windows. GPU: L*d small, O((Lx+Ly)d) per pair, ~minutes on the 8GB GPU via KeOps; subsample train to ~20k support paths.

all_candidates.method: Lead-lag signature transform on the cross-pair panel (signature-native lead-lag, depth-3 log-signature into GBM/SVM)
all_candidates.what: Apply the Hoff lead-lag transform (each 1-D path -> 2-D lead/lag staircase path) to the multi-pair returns, then take the truncated log-signature: the level-2 CROSS-TERMS between pair i's lead and pair j's lag directly encode the SIGNED quadratic-covariation / lead-lag rotation between pairs, and level-3 captures triadic ordering. Use the cross-terms as direction features and as a pairwise lead-lag metric for clustering which pair currently leads the USD move.
all_candidates.novelty: The repo's lead-lag work is LINEAR (lead-lag residuals, anti-contemporaneous lead-lag + transfer-entropy gate, DeltaLag-style). The Hoff lead-lag SIGNATURE transform is a different, nonlinear, reparametrization-invariant lead-lag encoding whose cross-terms recover volatility/quadratic-variation and signed lead-lag in one object; never applied here. And m30_sig.py's Lévy area was single-pair price-vs-OFI, NOT cross-pair lead-lag.
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (7 USD pairs, log-returns); 239-feat session/clock flags.
all_candidates.input_transform: For each NY-session window of L=20-30 1m bars: per pair, standardize log-returns -> cumulative path; apply lead-lag transform (interleave lead and lag samples, 2x length); stack the 7 lead-lag paths into one path and compute depth-2/3 log-signature via iisignature (CPU, pip-installable, light). Extract the antisymmetric cross-terms between {lead_i, lag_j} pairs as the lead-lag features (~21 ordered pairs * a few levels). Feed to LightGBM and to the sigkernel-SVM. De-overlap windows chrono; purge+embargo=1 horizon. Label = next-horizon EURUSD sign (and a USD-basket sign variant).

all_candidates.method: Randomized signatures (Cuchiero reservoir) as cheap fixed-dim path features for direction + gate
all_candidates.what: Compute a finite-dim randomized signature: a controlled ODE/recursion r_{t+1} = r_t + sum_k sigma(A_k r_t + b_k) dX^k_t with FROZEN random A_k,b_k, giving a ~100-300-dim state that provably approximates the full signature but is cheap and dimension-robust (avoids the factorial blowup of true signatures with d=8 channels). Use the final state as features into the existing GBM/meta-label gate.
all_candidates.novelty: True truncated signatures of a d=8 cross-pair path explode combinatorially (8^3 level-3 terms) — never feasible to try at depth>2, which is exactly why prior work stopped at level-2 single-pair. Randomized signatures sidestep this and were NEVER tried in the repo. They are the path-space analogue of the GRU/ESN reservoir already tried, but signature-grounded (different inductive bias: iterated-integral, reparametrization-invariant) rather than a generic recurrent reservoir.
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair 1m panel (8-channel path) for direction; OR single-pair (t, return, rv, OFI) path for the magnitude/gate.
all_candidates.input_transform: Form the increment stream dX_t over trailing L=30 bars with channels = (dt, 7 standardized pair log-returns) for the cross-sectional version, or (dt, log-ret, d rv_24, OFI) for the per-pair gate. Initialize r_0~N, draw A_k in R^{m x m} (m~256), b_k random, sigma=tanh; iterate the randomized-signature recursion over the window; take r_L (256-dim) as features. all_candidates.method: Gated DeltaNet as an online cross-sectional direction head (delta-rule = one SGD step of test-time training per bar)
all_candidates.what: Gated DeltaNet (ICLR 2025, improves Mamba-2 with the delta rule) maintains a matrix-valued fast-weight state updated per timestep by (a) a scalar data-dependent forget gate AND (b) a delta-rule write that REPLACES the value bound to the current key by an error-correcting amount. The write is provably one step of online SGD, so the recurrent state literally re-learns the key->value (regime->return) map at inference. We exploit this as built-in non-stationarity adaptation: the cross-pair USD-factor->next-return association is re-fit bar-by-bar without retraining.
all_candidates.novelty: Our tried list has Mamba/S4/S5 only as generic 'swap the backbone' levers and explicitly killed online Adaptive Random Forest as the online learner. Gated DeltaNet's delta-rule fast-weight (selective forget + error-correcting key overwrite, equivalent to test-time SGD on an associative memory) is a categorically different online-adaptation mechanism than ARF tree updates or recency-weighting (which we killed) and is NOT in the corpus (grep of _CORPUS_INDEX.md for deltanet/RWKV/retnet = 0 hits).

all_candidates.method: FASCL — Future-Aligned Soft Contrastive Learning on the 7-pair USD panel (cross-sectional, target-aware)
all_candidates.what: Train a per-bar encoder so embedding cosine-similarity between two pairs matches the SOFTMAX of their FUTURE forward-return correlation (KL-divergence loss), not their observed-window similarity. Pairs whose futures co-move get pulled together; the resulting embedding geometry encodes the USD-common-factor / lead-lag structure that is the certified direction edge — but supervised by the future instead of by augmentation.
all_candidates.novelty: Every SSL method we've cataloged (TS2Vec, TS-TCC, SimMTM, CoST, TNC) and every learned rep we've RUN (Kronos decode_s1, Chronos-2 group-attention) is SIGN-BLIND: positives come from augmentation/temporal-proximity/reconstruction, so the geometry never sees the forward return. FASCL (arXiv 2602.10711, Feb 2026) makes the SOFT TARGET the future-return correlation itself. Its ablation shows the observation-aligned variant (= SoftCLT, = what TS2Vec does) loses 3.3% vs future-aligned — i.e. the exact failure mode of our prior reps. Directly attacks the one place we have a real edge (cross-sectional) with a mechanism never in the repo (grep confirms zero contrastive impls).
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (features/<PAIR>_<year>.parquet for all 7 USD pairs; crosspair.py already builds the 5.3M-row aligned panel)
all_candidates.input_transform: Build per-(pair,bar) windows of L=64-128 bars of LOG-RETURNS (fractional-diff close, NOT raw levels — Chronos-2 failed precisely on levels) plus the OHLC-derived rv/rangepos/atr columns from the 239-store, RevIN-normalized per window. Encoder = small dilated-conv (TS2Vec backbone, ~1-2M params, runs on 8GB GPU). SOFT TARGET S_ij = Pearson corr of the FORWARD H-bar return series of pair i vs pair j over the horizon (H=15m/30m), restricted to the SAME timestamp (no look-ahead leak across instances: target built from t..t+H, embedding from t-L..t; purge t+H from train). Loss = KL(softmax(S_i/tau) || softmax(z_i·Z/tau)), NO projection head (their ablation: head costs -15.4%). all_candidates.what: Variational Mode Decomposition (or CEEMDAN) splits the trailing window into K band-limited intrinsic modes. Instead of the standard (leaky) 'decompose whole series -> predict each IMF', emit only CAUSAL summary stats of the trailing-window decomposition: per-mode energy fraction, instantaneous frequency of the dominant mode, high-vs-low-freq energy ratio. These describe the current scale-mix of the move.
all_candidates.novelty: Corpus has EMD2FNN (whole-series, leaky, generic 'EMD denoise') only. Two novelties: (a) VMD specifically (mode-mixing-free, mathematically rigorous vs EMD) is not cataloged; (b) the strictly-causal, summary-stat-only, NO-RECONSTRUCTION formulation sidesteps the exact lookahead-leakage the corpus's wavelet-denoise warning flags — most published decompose-then-predict pipelines leak; this one does not.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1m close per-pair; 1s tick for a microstructure-scale variant.
all_candidates.input_transform: Per bar t, trailing window W=256 of log-returns. Run VMD (vmdpy, K=4-6 modes, alpha~2000) on that window ONLY. Emit: energy fraction of each mode, ratio of high-freq (mode K) to low-freq (mode 1) energy, and the Hilbert instantaneous frequency of the dominant mode (causal). These become regime/gate features (trending vs choppy scale-mix) appended to the 243-feat store. Never reconstruct or feed future IMF values. Re-run window each bar (recompute VMD is the cost; W=256, K=5 is ~ms on CPU). CEEMDAN variant via PyEMD for robustness check.
all_candidates.falsifier: Pre-register: VMD energy-ratio gate must lift the direction up-rate in its best bucket past breakeven on purged OOS while passing the moved-bars [.47,.53] tripwire, OR add >=0.01 magnitude AUC. Per-window VMD instability (mode count flips across adjacent bars producing noisy features, |lag-1 autocorr of feature| < 0.3) is an automatic KILL.

all_candidates.method: Per-pair Fixed-Width Fractional Differencing (FFD) BEFORE the cross-pair USD-residual
all_candidates.what: Apply Lopez-de-Prado FFD with the minimum d* (ADF-stationary) to each pair's log-price, preserving long memory that integer-differencing to returns destroys, THEN form the USD-common-factor / USD-residual on the fractionally-differenced series. The certified cross-sectional edge is currently built on (memory-destroying) returns; FFD keeps the persistent level information that may carry the cross-pair lead-lag signal.
all_candidates.novelty: FFD is cataloged generically as a univariate stationarity transform, but it has NEVER been composed with the certified cross-pair USD-residual / lead-lag pipeline — which is the ONLY certified direction edge. The hypothesis is specific: the cross-sectional edge lives in shared persistent (memory) components that d=1 returns discard. That composition is untried.
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair aligned 1m panel (7 USD pairs), per-pair 1m close.
all_candidates.input_transform: For each of the 7 pairs: compute FFD weights for a grid of d in [0.1..0.9], pick d* = smallest d passing ADF on the in-sample (train-only) era, fix the fixed-width window (weights below tol dropped). Produce ffd_t = sum_k w_k * log(close_{t-k}) (causal). Build the cross-pair common factor (first PC / cross-sectional mean) on the 7 FFD series and the per-pair FFD-residual = ffd_pair - loading*factor. Feed these residuals (+ their lead-lag at 1-3 bars) to the existing cross-pair direction GBM in place of / alongside return-residuals. Tune d* ONCE on train, freeze for OOS (no per-fold refit of d to avoid leakage).
all_candidates.falsifier: Pre-register: FFD-residual cross-section must beat the return-residual cross-section CPCV p10 at 10m/15m (current p10 ~.57-.61) on purged OOS, NY-session-concentrated. If FFD-residual p10 <= return-residual p10 across all d* tested -> KILL (memory adds nothing to the cross-section).
all_candidates.source: Lopez de Prado AFML ch5 (FFD); lib: fracdiff (github fracdiff/fracdiff), mlfinlab frac_diff; cross-sectional composition is the novel step

all_candidates.method: Maximal-Overlap Discrete Wavelet Scattering Transform (MODWST) front-end for the data-scarce cross-pair direction head
all_candidates.what: Combine MODWT (shift-invariant, any-length, no decimation) with the scattering wavelet transform to produce translation-invariant, stable multi-scale features that the 2025 paper shows BEAT CNNs specifically when training data is LIMITED. Our certified cross-pair edge is regime/session-concentrated (NY only) and per-regime data-scarce — exactly MODWST's claimed sweet spot.
all_candidates.novelty: MODWST (arXiv 2506.12039, 2025) is a brand-new transform absent from the corpus. Unlike plain DWT denoising (cataloged), MODWST is undecimated (shift-invariant -> robust to where the window ends) and adds the scattering nonlinearity (modulus + 2nd wavelet) -> a representation distinct from both the cataloged wavelet-denoise and from learned CNNs (which we already tried and which underperform on limited data).
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1m close per-pair / cross-pair panel; usable on 1s tick window.
all_candidates.input_transform: Trailing causal window of log-returns (length need not be 2^k since MODWT is any-length), e.g. 256 1m bars. Apply MODWT (pywt SWT / 'modwt' pkg) to get undecimated detail coeffs per scale, take modulus, apply a second MODWT, average -> MODWST coefficient vector (~ a few dozen dims). Build these per pair, difference vs USD-mean for the cross-section, and feed to the existing GBM direction head (small, leakage-safe, no extra net to train). Because it is shift-invariant, the feature at bar t is stable to the exact window boundary -> less noisy than decimated DWT features.
all_candidates.falsifier: Pre-register: MODWST cross-pair features must hold CPCV p10 >= 0.541 (ideally >= current .57) on purged NY-session OOS at 10m/15m and beat plain DWT-coefficient features head-to-head. If MODWST <= plain-DWT and <= return-residual baseline -> KILL.
all_candidates.source: arXiv:2506.12039 'The Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Scattering Transform and Its Application in Classification Tasks' (2025); MODWT via pywt/'modwt' pkg, scattering via kymatio

all_candidates.method: HARQ — realized-quarticity attenuation correction on rv30/rv120
all_candidates.what: Bollerslev-Patton-Quaedvlieg HARQ: let the AR coefficient on each realized-vol lag scale with that lag's measurement noise, proxied by realized quarticity RQ (the 'vol-of-vol', mean of r^4). When RQ is high the rv estimate is noisy, so the model down-weights it (corrects attenuation bias), sharpening the prediction of the abnormal/large-move component exactly where our magnitude target lives.
all_candidates.novelty: We use rv30/rv120 as RAW level regressors fed to LightGBM. We have NEVER computed realized quarticity, nor the RQ-interaction (rv * sqrt(RQ)) that is the whole point of HARQ. rv != RQ; RQ is the 4th-moment noise proxy, a genuinely new feature family. FX-specific validation exists (AIMS 2024 'relevance of realized quarticity for exchange rate volatility forecasts').
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1-min OHLCV (close) per pair — already on disk; optionally 1s tick (EURUSD) for higher-fidelity intraday RQ.
all_candidates.input_transform: Per decision bar i and horizon H (30/120 min): from 1-min log-returns r build RV_w = sum_{j in w} r_j^2 over windows w in {30,120,daily} (matches existing rv30/rv120^2), and RQ_w = (N_w/3)*sum r_j^4. For the 1s tick file, compute the same with 60 sub-returns/min for a cleaner RQ. New features to ADD on top of [-pe,rv30,rv120]: RQ30, RQ120, sqrt(RQ30), and the HARQ interaction terms rv30*sqrt(RQ30), rv120*sqrt(RQ120). Stationarity already handled (returns/variances). Feed all to the SAME certified LightGBM + CPCV pipeline (deseason_mag.py harness) so it is a paired add-on test vs the rv baseline.
all_candidates.falsifier: Pre-register: ADD {RQ30,RQ120,sqrt(RQ),rv*sqrt(RQ)} to the certified feature set; KILL if path-mean 30m magAUC does not exceed the rv-baseline path-mean by >= +0.003 with frac_clear staying 1.0 at cov<=10% on the 28 purged CPCV paths (same bar as deseason_mag MAG_BAR=0.55). Also kill if SHAP shows RQ terms rank below rv30 AND the lift is within CPCV path-std.

all_candidates.method: Guyon-Lekeufack Path-Dependent Volatility features (R1 trend + R2 activity, time-shifted power-law kernels)
all_candidates.what: Model instantaneous vol as a linear combo of R1 = a kernel-weighted sum of PAST SIGNED returns (a trend/leverage feature) and R2 = sqrt of a kernel-weighted sum of PAST SQUARED returns (an activity feature), each with a time-shifted power-law (TSPL) kernel. Guyon-Lekeufack show R1,R2 explain ~65% of future daily RV out-of-sample, beating HAR — and crucially R1 (the SIGNED leverage term) is a magnitude feature that carries directional information.
all_candidates.novelty: Our rv30/rv120 are symmetric, single-scale rolling stds with implicit equal weights and NO signed-trend term. The TSPL-kernel R1 (signed, leverage) and the power-law-weighted R2 are a distinct, continuous-memory parameterization never tried. R1 is the first magnitude feature in our program that is SIGN-sensitive — a possible bridge from the magnitude edge into the unsolved DOWN direction side.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1-min OHLCV close per pair (on disk). No tick data needed.
all_candidates.input_transform: From 1-min log-returns r_t: build TSPL kernel K_a(tau)=(tau+delta)^{-a} (or the exact Guyon shifted-power-law) over a long lookback (e.g. last 1000-4000 min, ~3-10 trading days). R1_t = sum_tau K_{a1}(tau)*r_{t-tau}  (signed → trend/leverage). R2_t = sqrt( sum_tau K_{a2}(tau)*r_{t-tau}^2 ) (activity). Compute 2-3 kernel-speed pairs (fast/slow a) to mimic HAR multiscale. All causal (only past). ADD {R1_fast,R1_slow,R2_fast,R2_slow, R1*R2} as features to the certified LightGBM+CPCV magnitude pipeline; ALSO test R1 alone as a feature in the cross-pair DIRECTION book (its signed-leverage content).

all_candidates.method: Realized semivariance + signed jump variation (good-vol / bad-vol decomposition)
all_candidates.what: Barndorff-Nielsen RS-/RS+ split RV into downside (negative-return) and upside (positive-return) parts; Patton-Sheppard signed jump SJ = RS+ - RS-. Empirically negative semivariance/negative jumps predict HIGHER future vol than positive — an asymmetry that (a) improves magnitude forecasts and (b) is directionally informative (sign realized jump risk explains cross-sectional returns).
all_candidates.novelty: Our rv30/rv120 are symmetric — they THROW AWAY the sign of the within-window returns. RS+, RS-, and SJ are never computed. This is the cleanest, lowest-cost asymmetry feature and is the strongest documented MAGNITUDE→DIRECTION bridge in the cluster: SJ is sign-carrying yet built from a magnitude decomposition, so it can be tested on BOTH targets including the unsolved DOWN side and the NY cross-pair book.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1-min OHLCV close per pair (on disk); 1s tick (EURUSD) for sharper jump detection.
all_candidates.input_transform: Within each rolling window w (30,120 min): from 1-min returns r_j, RS+_w = sum r_j^2 * 1[r_j>0], RS-_w = sum r_j^2 * 1[r_j<0]; SJ_w = RS+_w - RS-_w; and the asymmetry ratio RS-_w/RV_w. For jumps: use bipower variation BPV = (pi/2)*sum|r_j||r_{j-1}| (continuous part) and jump J_w = max(RV_w - BPV_w, 0); signed jump = sign of cumulative return * J. ADD {RS+,RS-,SJ,RS-/RV,J30,J120} to the magnitude LightGBM+CPCV pipeline. SEPARATELY: cross-sectionally rank SJ across the 7 USD pairs (panel) and feed the rank as a feature in the NY cross-pair DIRECTION book.
all_candidates.falsifier: MAGNITUDE kill: {RS+,RS-,SJ,J} add < +0.003 to 30m path-mean magAUC (paired CPCV). DIRECTION kill: cross-sectional SJ rank adds < +0.005 to NY cross-pair UP or DOWN p10 (cert 15/15 intact). Also kill SJ-for-direction if the sign of its coefficient flips across the 28 paths (unstable).

The continuous part is highly persistent (drives future size); jumps are transient. CHAR (replace RV with BPV in HAR) is a documented benchmark that the rv-only model omits.
all_candidates.novelty: rv30/rv120 lump jumps and diffusion together. We have never separated BPV (jump-robust diffusion estimator) from the jump component, nor tested whether the CONTINUOUS part alone is a cleaner predictor of large forward moves. Distinct from CCM/perm-entropy/OFI lines already killed.

all_candidates.method: Multivariate fractional Brownian motion (mfBM) cross-pair rough-vol forecaster
all_candidates.what: Model the 7-pair vector of log realized variances as a multivariate fractional Brownian motion: each pair has a rough Hurst H~0.1, plus a CROSS-pair fractional covariance structure. The conditional-expectation forecast borrows strength across pairs (a USD-common rough-vol factor), which the paper shows beats univariate HAR and univariate rough-vol given the strong cross-RV correlation.
all_candidates.novelty: Our cross-pair edge work is all DIRECTION (USD-residual/OFI/lead-lag/IPCA). We have NEVER modeled the cross-pair MAGNITUDE panel jointly, and never used a rough (H<0.5, fractional) memory structure on log-RV. Rough vol / fractional OU is explicitly on the not-tried list; the multivariate cross-RV coupling is the magnitude analogue of our certified cross-pair direction edge.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (5.3M rows, all 7 USD pairs, on disk).
all_candidates.input_transform: Build per-pair log-RV series: logRV_{p,t} = log(sum of 1-min r^2 over the 30m window) for each pair p. Estimate per-pair Hurst H_p via the m=1,2 absolute-moment / variance-of-log-RV-increments regression (Gatheral-Jaisson-Rosenbaum estimator) on the TRAIN block ONLY (leakage guard). Fit the mfBM cross-covariance (correlation of fractional log-RV innovations across pairs). Forecast EURUSD's H-step log-RV as the mfBM conditional expectation using ALL 7 pairs' recent log-RV. Feed the forecast (and the per-pair H, and the cross-pair RV factor = first PC of the 7 log-RVs) as features into the certified magnitude pipeline. Strict per-CPCV-path Hurst/covariance estimation.

all_candidates.method: Time-augmented + lead-lag PATH SIGNATURE features for the magnitude target (SignatureHAR)
all_candidates.what: Lift the recent price/return path to a time-augmented, lead-lag transformed rough path and compute its truncated signature (iterated integrals). Level-2 signature terms recover QUADRATIC VARIATION (volatility); the off-diagonal Levy-area terms encode time-asymmetry/leverage. Use these signature coordinates as features (SignatureHAR), which capture multiscale path information HAR/rv cannot.

The signature's quadratic-variation level is a principled, model-free magnitude feature; the Levy-area level is a directional-asymmetry feature — another magnitude→direction bridge, and the lead-lag construction directly encodes cross-pair lead-lag for the cross-sectional edge.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1-min OHLCV close (on disk); 1s tick (EURUSD) for finer paths; cross-pair panel for the multi-channel lead-lag lift.
all_candidates.input_transform: Per decision bar, take the last L 1-min log-prices (e.g. L=60-120). Form a 2-channel path X_t=(t/L, cumlogret_t) (time-augmentation). all_candidates.method: Realized-GARCH / HEAVY as a confidence GATE (predicted-vol-conditional reliability)
all_candidates.what: Fit a Realized-GARCH or HEAVY model jointly on daily returns + the realized measure to get a forward conditional-vol path with a measurement-equation residual that quantifies how RELIABLE the realized measure currently is. Use the predicted conditional vol (and its measurement-error variance) as a GATE: only trade the certified direction/magnitude book when forward vol is in the reliable regime — a principled replacement for the bb_width-compression gate.
all_candidates.novelty: Our gating is bb_width x session x confidence (tree-based). Realized-GARCH/HEAVY's joint return+realized-measure recursion and its measurement-equation error variance (the attenuation signal) are never used as a gate. Distinct from HMM regime gating already in the catalog.

all_candidates.input_transform: Aggregate 1-min to the decision frequency. Realized measure x_t = RV over the prior window (the rv we already have). Output forward h_t and the standardized measurement residual as a GATE feature: define 'reliable' = predicted h in a mid-band AND |u_t| small. Apply the gate ON TOP of the certified direction book (keep only gated rows) and re-score p10.

all_candidates.method: TICC (Toeplitz Inverse-Covariance Clustering) on the cross-pair return panel — regime = which lead-lag/correlation MRF is active
all_candidates.what: TICC segments a multivariate series into states, each DEFINED by a sparse Toeplitz inverse-covariance (a time-lagged Markov random field over the 7 pairs). Instead of vol regimes, the state IS the cross-pair correlation/lead-lag structure — exactly where our only certified direction edge lives. Condition the cross-pair sign model (or its sign) per active correlation-regime.
all_candidates.novelty: Our tried HMM (min1_hmm.py / METHODS_CATALOG C1) used a Gaussian emission HMM that collapsed to PURE VOL regimes (P(up)=0.497-0.499 in every state, zero sign lift). TICC clusters on the INVERSE-COVARIANCE / cross-correlation graph, not on marginal mean/vol, so its regimes partition the panel by *dependency topology* (which pair leads which). Never implemented; corpus has 0 TICC levers. Distinct from IPCA/USD-residual (those are static factor models, not a regime switch over the dependency graph).
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (5.3M rows, built by m5_xpair.py over EURUSD,GBPUSD,AUDUSD,NZDUSD,USDJPY,USDCHF,USDCAD); per-pair features/<PAIR>_<year>.parquet.
all_candidates.input_transform: Build the multivariate window TICC expects: at each minute t form the 7-vector of log-returns r_t=log(close_t/close_{t-1}) for the 7 pairs (USDJPY etc. already USD-quote consistent; invert non-USD-base pairs so all are USD-strength-signed). Standardize per-pair on TRAIN only. TICC's window size w = the lag-depth of the MRF — set w=10-30 min (the lead-lag scale we found at >=10m). Resample to 5-min bars to cut rows (~1M) for the laptop. Fit TICC (K=3-5, sparsity lambda, temporal-smoothness beta) on TRAIN via its ADMM/EM; assign held-out minutes the state by the CAUSAL forward log-likelihood of the most-recent w-window (NOT the smoothed/Viterbi label — same leakage discipline as min1_hmm._forward_filter). Use the hard state + soft posteriors as (a) a gate on the certified m10/m15 cross-pair book (trade only in states where it clears BE on worst-VAL-half) and (b) extra meta-features. pip: install TICC (Stanford reference impl) or reimplement ADMM (~200 lines).
all_candidates.falsifier: Pre-register: KILL if no TICC state has P(cross-pair-book-correct) >= 0.555 on the worst-VAL-half AND CPCV p10 over the gated subset < 0.541; or if the inferred states are >0.9-rank-correlated with rv (i.e. it rediscovered vol regimes, repeating the HMM failure).

all_candidates.method: Cross-sectional-dependence change-point detection (sequential empirical-copula / equicorrelation-breakdown) as a direction gate on the cross-pair panel
all_candidates.what: A change-point test built on the sequential empirical COPULA process detects a break in the *dependence* among the 7 pairs (not the marginals). The run-length / time-since-last-dependence-break, and the sign of the equicorrelation jump, become a conditioning variable: the cross-pair common-factor sign edge is strongest right when dependence is HIGH/just re-coupled, and breaks down when correlations fracture.
all_candidates.novelty: We have catalogued 'regime conditioning' vaguely but never a dependence-structure (copula) change-point test. Our cross-pair edge work (USD-residual, IPCA, lead-lag) all assumes a STABLE dependence; this explicitly detects WHEN that dependence breaks and gates around it. Corpus levers on 'cross-sectional dependence change-point' = 0 implemented. Orthogonal to bb_width/session gating (those are univariate vol/clock, this is the 7-pair copula).
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (m5_xpair.py); the certified cross-pair direction books EURUSD.m10xp.v1 / m15xp.v1.
all_candidates.input_transform: Resample the 7 USD-signed log-return series to the trade horizon's bar (10m/15m). Maintain a rolling window (e.g. last N=200 bars). Compute (i) Dynamic Equicorrelation rho_t (Engle-Kelly: average pairwise corr) and (ii) a CAUSAL sequential-empirical-copula CUSUM statistic on the window (rank-transform each pair within the window, accumulate the empirical-copula deviation). Declare a dependence break when the CUSUM crosses a TRAIN-calibrated threshold. Derive 3 causal features per bar: rho_t level, sign(d rho_t), and bars-since-last-break. Gate: only take the certified cross-pair sign when rho_t is in the high tercile AND no break in the last K bars (states learned on VAL). All thresholds/terciles fit on TRAIN only; evaluate gated subset under CPCV.
all_candidates.falsifier: KILL if gating on rho-tercile x no-recent-break does not lift the cross-pair book's worst-VAL-half win-rate by >=0.8pp, or if CPCV p10 on the gated subset <= the ungated p10 (already certified ~.57-.59). Also kill if rho_t is monotone with our existing bb_width gate (redundant).
all_candidates.source: Bucher/Kojadinovic/Rohmer, 'Detecting changes in cross-sectional dependence in multivariate time series', arXiv:1206.2557; Engle & Kelly, 'Dynamic Equicorrelation', NYU 2008

all_candidates.method: Markov-Switching Multifractal (MSM, Calvet-Fisher) as the magnitude / volatility forecaster
all_candidates.what: MSM models volatility as the product of many independent two-state multipliers with heterogeneous (geometrically-spaced) switching frequencies — a parsimonious multi-scale regime cascade. It produces a forward conditional-vol forecast that, in FX, beats GARCH/MS-GARCH/FIGARCH out-of-sample at medium horizons.
all_candidates.novelty: Our magnitude edge uses rv30/rv120 (rolling std) + time-of-day; permutation entropy was NULL. MSM is a DIFFERENT volatility-generating mechanism (multiplicative multi-frequency cascade with closed-form multi-step forecasts), NOT a rolling realized-vol stat, and is explicitly documented to out-forecast GARCH-class on FX volatility. Never tried (corpus has Markov-switching as a vague concept, 0 MSM levers; we only tried realized-vol features).
all_candidates.required_inputs: Per-pair 1-min OHLCV close (features/<PAIR>_<year>.parquet); the certified 30m magnitude target |fwd ret| and its rv baseline.
all_candidates.input_transform: Take log-returns r_t at the magnitude horizon's bar (resample 1m close to 30m). Demean. Fit MSM with kbar=4-8 multipliers via the GMM or ML (binomial multiplier m0, switching base gamma_1, frequency b) on TRAIN. The model gives E[sigma_{t+1}|info_t] — a multi-scale conditional-vol forecast. Add log(sigma_MSM,t) as a feature ALONGSIDE rv30/rv120/time-of-day in the certified magnitude GBM, and separately test it standalone vs the rv baseline. Multi-step: MSM has analytic h-step vol forecasts, so it natively predicts |30m ret| from a 1m-fit. CPU-cheap (few params). Library: MSM via `pip install` not standard — use the R `MSGARCH`/Matlab Calvet-Fisher code or a ~150-line numpy ML fit.
all_candidates.falsifier: KILL if log(sigma_MSM) does not beat the rv30/rv120 baseline on purged OOS magnitude AUC (must exceed the certified .744->.758 with-clock number when added, or beat rv standalone), OR if its SHAP contribution alongside rv is <1% (subsumed by realized vol, like Kronos-dispersion was).

all_candidates.method: BOCPD with autoregressive, time-varying-parameter segments (Bayesian run-length) as a magnitude regime-clock + direction gate
all_candidates.what: Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection maintains the full posterior over run-length (time since last regime break). The 2024 autoregressive/score-driven variant (ARVC-BOCPD) lets each segment be an AR process with within-segment drifting variance/correlation — so the run-length posterior tracks both mean and dependence breaks online, causally, with a forecast distribution.
all_candidates.novelty: Listed as an aspiration in IDEAS_LOG #24 but NEVER implemented (corpus has 1 BOCPD lever, descriptive only). The 2024 AR + time-varying-param extension (arXiv:2407.16376) is strictly richer than vanilla BOCPD (which we also never ran) and gives a calibrated run-length posterior usable as a continuous gate, not a hard segmentation. Distinct from HMM: BOCPD is non-parametric in #states and gives an explicit P(regime just changed) each bar.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Per-pair 1-min close (features parquets) for the trade pair; 1s tick (features_tick) optionally for finer run-length at sub-minute.
all_candidates.input_transform: Feed the AR-BOCPD a univariate causal stream: log-returns at the trade-horizon bar (or rv-deseasonalized returns to remove the intraday seasonality we already exploit). Run BOCPD forward-only (it is inherently online — no leakage). Each bar emits: P(run-length=0) (=break prob), E[run-length], and the posterior predictive vol. Use (a) E[run-length] / break-prob as a magnitude feature (vol mean-reverts after breaks) and (b) a DIRECTION gate: suppress trades in the first K bars after a high-prob change-point (regime just flipped = sign least stable), which the binding-regime wall in IDEAS_LOG suggests is exactly where the cross-pair sign gets erased. Calibrate hazard rate lambda on TRAIN (the 2025 paper found lambda~100 optimal on daily; scale to bar count). Library: github.com/HolyBayes/klcpd has BOCPD utilities, or hazard+studentT BOCPD is ~80 lines.
all_candidates.falsifier: KILL for direction if excluding the K-bar post-changepoint window does not raise the cross-pair book worst-VAL-half win-rate by >=0.5pp (i.e. breaks don't precede sign-erasure). KILL for magnitude if break-prob/run-length adds <1% SHAP over rv and time-of-day on purged OOS.

all_candidates.method: Wavelet-leader jump separation by time-asymmetry — directional jump labeling of training bars (PNAS 2024)
all_candidates.what: A 2024 PNAS method uses the time-ASYMMETRY of the wavelet response around a shock to separate/classify price jumps into distinct classes. The asymmetry (whether the build-up vs relaxation around the shock is faster) is a SIGNED, directional descriptor of how the move formed — unlike symmetric realized-jump (bipower) measures.
all_candidates.novelty: We tried jump-FILTER relabeling (bipower/RV divergence) but those are SIGN-INVARIANT (semivariance is symmetric). Wavelet-leader TIME-ASYMMETRY is a genuinely directional shock descriptor and is NOT in our tried list (Bandt-Pompe signed-ordinal was killed but that's ordinal-pattern, not wavelet-asymmetry). Multifractal/wavelet-leader has 3 corpus mentions, all as vol descriptors, none as a directional jump classifier or a label.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick mid (features_tick/{train,val,test,oos}_1s.parquet, EURUSD) for high-res shocks; 1m close for coarser. Per-pair parquets for cross-pair extension.
all_candidates.input_transform: On the 1s (or 1m) mid-price, compute the discrete wavelet transform and its wavelet LEADERS (local sup of |coeffs| over finer scales) in a causal trailing window around each candidate shock. Detect shocks as leader-coefficient exceedances. For each detected shock compute the time-asymmetry statistic (ratio of pre- vs post-shock leader decay, computed CAUSALLY using only the trailing leaders that have completed). Use it two ways: (1) LABEL filter — train the direction model only on bars belonging to the asymmetry-class that empirically precedes a continuation vs reversal (learned on TRAIN), evaluated on TRUE forward sign; (2) FEATURE — the signed asymmetry as a microstructure input to the gate. Strictly causal: only past-and-current scales (the leader at scale j is available once j-scale window has elapsed). Library: pywt for DWT/leaders, ~150 lines for the asymmetry stat.
all_candidates.falsifier: KILL if the time-asymmetry class shows no >=2pp forward-sign-rate separation between classes on TRAIN holdout, OR if the asymmetry feature is computable only with future scales (leakage — the PNAS framing is partly retrospective; if the causal-only version loses the signal, kill).
all_candidates.source: 'Identifying new classes of financial price jumps with wavelets', PNAS 2024, doi:10.1073/pnas.2409156121 (PMC11831140); Wendt-Abry wavelet leaders multifractal formalism

all_candidates.method: Sticky HDP-HSMM (Bayesian-nonparametric, explicit-duration regimes) for magnitude-regime conditioning
all_candidates.what: HDP-HSMM infers the NUMBER of regimes from data and replaces the HMM's geometric (memoryless) dwell-time with an explicit duration distribution + a 'sticky' self-transition prior, so regimes persist realistically instead of flickering. The posterior dwell/duration and state-vol become a conditioning variable for magnitude (and a stability check for the direction gate).
all_candidates.novelty: Our HMM was a FIXED-K Gaussian HMM with geometric dwell, which produced flickering pure-vol states. HDP-HSMM (a) learns K, (b) imposes explicit duration so regimes are persistent (addressing the 'states flicker / VAL-OOS anti-transfer' failure noted in usdjpy_2m), and (c) sticky bias prevents over-segmentation. Corpus: 1 sticky lever (a microstructure pinned-mid detector, unrelated), 0 HDP-HSMM. Genuinely new mechanism vs tried HMM.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Per-pair 1-min features (rv_12, rv_24, atr, bb_width, signed multi-tf returns) from features/<PAIR>_<year>.parquet.
all_candidates.input_transform: Build the emission vector exactly as min1_hmm did (signed returns + rv + flow: ret60/ret300/rv300/imb) but resampled to ~5-min grid (regimes persist >> bar). Fit a WEAK-LIMIT sticky HDP-HSMM (truncated, e.g. Lmax=8) with a negative-binomial duration prior and kappa (stickiness) tuned on TRAIN, via pyhsmm (github.com/mattjj/pyhsmm, CPU, the original Johnson-Willsky impl). Assign held-out bars by the CAUSAL forward message (left-to-right HSMM filter, not the backward/Viterbi). Use posterior state-vol + dwell as magnitude features and as a 'regime maturity' gate (trade direction only mid-regime, not in the first/last few bars of a state). Compare its inferred K and dwell to the tried HMM to confirm it is NOT just relabeling the same vol states.
all_candidates.falsifier: KILL if the inferred states are again pure-vol (P(up) within 0.49-0.51 each) — the same failure as the Gaussian HMM (this is the pre-committed null; if explicit-duration + nonparametric K does not change the sign-content, the whole HMM family is confirmed dead for direction). For magnitude, kill if posterior state-vol adds <1% over rv30/rv120.
all_candidates.source: Johnson & Willsky, 'Bayesian Nonparametric Hidden Semi-Markov Models', JMLR 2013, arXiv:1203.1365; Fox et al. sticky HDP-HMM; pyhsmm library

all_candidates.method: Cross-sectional VPIN (order-flow toxicity) divergence as a NY-session direction gate + feature, across all 7 USD pairs
all_candidates.what: VPIN = volume-synchronized probability of informed trading: bucket flow into equal-volume buckets, classify each bucket's volume into buy/sell via Bulk Volume Classification (BVC: buy-fraction = Phi(standardized bucket return)), and set VPIN = rolling mean of |V_buy - V_sell|/V. High toxicity flags an asymmetric-information episode where one side persistently dominates; the SIGN of the BVC buy/sell imbalance during a high-VPIN window carries the directional lean that ordinary symmetric flow does not.
all_candidates.novelty: Already-tried list has OFI/cross-impact/xofi/transfer-entropy but NOT VPIN, NOT the volume-clock (equal-volume buckets) construction, and NOT Bulk Volume Classification of volume into buy/sell. VPIN is a volume-clock toxicity measure (Easley-Lopez de Prado-O'Hara) distinct from the time-clock OFI proxies already killed. The cross-pair toxicity-divergence framing (which of the 7 USD pairs is most toxic right now -> that pair's USD-leg leads) is a new cross-sectional direction channel.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick store (mid, tsz volume, imb) for the cross-pair-relevant horizon; raw tick bid-vol/ask-vol for all 7 pairs in /media/sean/CORSAIR/tick_data/raw/<PAIR>/ to build per-pair VPIN.
all_candidates.input_transform: Per pair: from the 1s store, form a volume clock by cumulating tsz into equal-volume buckets (bucket size = median daily volume / 50). Within each bucket compute standardized bucket log-return z = dP/(sigma_bucket); BVC buy-volume = V*Phi(z), sell = V*(1-Phi(z)). VPIN_pair = mean over last n=50 buckets of |2*buyfrac-1|. Signed-toxicity = VPIN_pair * sign(sum buy-sell over window). Build the 7-pair signed-toxicity vector, project onto USD via the +1/-1 quote convention (JPY/CHF/CAD inverted), take the USD-common toxicity factor (mean) and EURUSD-idiosyncratic toxicity residual. Feed VPIN level (gate: trade only when EURUSD VPIN in top quartile = informed regime), signed-toxicity residual (direction feature), and cross-pair toxicity dispersion into the existing cross-pair direction GBM, resampled to the model's bar grid (1m/5m). Restrict to NY session where the certified edge lives.
all_candidates.falsifier: On purged CPCV OOS, the high-VPIN-quartile subset's EURUSD direction AUC does NOT exceed 0.541 breakeven AND the signed-toxicity residual's standalone direction AUC <= 0.52 (i.e., VPIN only marks magnitude/vol regime, not sign) -> kill. Pre-register: also require VPIN-gated up-rate of moved bars stays in [.47,.53] (no leakage).
all_candidates.source: Easley, Lopez de Prado, O'Hara 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High Frequency World' (RFS 2012); Easley et al. 'Bulk Volume Classification' / 'Discerning Information from Trade Data' (JFE 2016); stern.nyu.edu/.../con_035928.pdf

all_candidates.method: Kyle's lambda (price-impact slope) as a depth/illiquidity REGIME feature for magnitude + a confidence GATE for direction
all_candidates.what: Kyle lambda = regression slope of signed price change on signed order flow over a rolling window (dP = lambda * signed_flow + eps); it measures adverse-selection/market depth (illiquidity). High lambda = thin, information-sensitive market where the same flow moves price more -> larger forthcoming |return| (magnitude) and a regime where directional flow signals are most reliable (gate).
all_candidates.novelty: Cross-impact matrix and OFI were tried but Kyle lambda as an explicitly ESTIMATED rolling impact-slope (a per-bar regression coefficient, not a flow level) is not in the tried list. It is the natural inverse-depth scaler the corpus index flagged as untried ('OFI->impact slope INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL TO MARKET DEPTH ... depth-adaptive feature'). Used as a MAGNITUDE regressor (depth predicts move size) and a DIRECTION gate (trust flow-sign only when lambda is high), neither of which we have run.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick store (mid for dP, signed flow from imb*tsz or BVC-signed volume); per-pair raw tick for cross-pair lambda.
all_candidates.input_transform: Signed flow per 1s bar f_t = imb_t * tsz_t (or BVC-signed tsz). Over a rolling 5-min window regress (mid_t - mid_{t-1}) on f_t with no intercept -> lambda_t (use Theil-Sen/robust slope to resist outliers). Also build Amihud-style |ret|/tsz as a cheaper illiquidity twin. Resample lambda_t, its log, and its rolling z-score to the magnitude model's 30m grid; ADD to the certified rv30/rv120 + time-of-day magnitude feature set (does lambda lift 30m mag AUC above the .744->.758 baseline?). Separately feed lambda's rolling quantile as a binary gate to the direction model: enable cross-pair direction trade only in top-tercile-lambda bars.

all_candidates.method: Bulk Volume Classification (BVC) signed-flow imbalance as a NEW direction feature replacing the quote-size imb proxy
all_candidates.what: Our existing 'imb' is bid-vol/ask-vol QUOTE-size imbalance, not trade-sign flow. BVC re-classifies each volume bar's volume into buyer- vs seller-initiated using the standardized-return CDF (buyfrac = Phi(dP/sigma)), giving a probabilistic AGGRESSOR-side imbalance that is documented to be better-linked to information-based trading than the tick rule or raw quote imbalance — a genuinely different signed-flow series for the direction model.
all_candidates.novelty: The tried list uses OFI proxies and quote-imbalance (imb); BVC is a distinct, untried trade-classification that turns volume into signed aggressor flow via the return-distribution CDF and needs no true trade signs (perfect for our async Dukascopy ticks that lack a trade-sign field). 'Count-based vs size-based OFI' is cataloged but BVC's Phi(z)-weighted classification is not.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick store (mid for dP, tsz for volume) per pair; raw tick to refine bucket sigma.
all_candidates.input_transform: Per 1s (or per equal-volume bucket): dP = log(mid_t/mid_{t-1}); sigma = rolling std of dP over ~60 bars; buyvol = tsz*Phi(dP/sigma); netflow = 2*buyvol - tsz. Aggregate netflow to the model bar (sum within bar), normalize by bar volume -> BVC_imbalance in [-1,1]. Build the 7-pair BVC vector, extract USD-common BVC factor and EURUSD-idiosyncratic BVC residual (same projection as the certified USD-residual pipeline). Feed BVC residual + lags (1,2,3,5,10 bars) into the cross-pair direction GBM alongside (NOT replacing, then ablating) the existing OFI proxies, NY-session-restricted.

all_candidates.method: Hayashi-Yoshida asynchronous lead-lag cross-correlation -> adaptive cross-pair lag alignment for the certified cross-sectional edge
all_candidates.what: Hayashi-Yoshida estimates the correlation/lead-lag between two ASYNCHRONOUSLY-sampled tick series using all overlapping tick-interval products, without resampling to a common grid. Sweeping a lag offset gives a HY cross-correlogram whose argmax = the data-driven lead-lag (in seconds) of one USD pair over another. Use the discovered per-pair lag to LAG-ALIGN leader-pair flows before they enter the EURUSD direction model.
all_candidates.novelty: Lead-lag residuals and anti-contemporaneous lead-lag with TE gate were tried, but those used FIXED-grid resampled returns at fixed lags. HY operates on the raw irregular tick timestamps (our ticks arrive at 2/sec with gaps) and recovers a CONTINUOUS, time-varying optimal lag in seconds that fixed-bar lead-lag cannot see (the corpus explicitly notes HY 'partially solves spurious lead-lag from regularly sampled data'). The adaptive-lag alignment of leader flows is the new mechanism.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Raw tick mid for all 7 pairs (/media/sean/CORSAIR/tick_data/raw/<PAIR>/), with native irregular timestamps.
all_candidates.input_transform: For each ordered pair (leader L, EURUSD), keep native tick log-returns with their timestamps (do NOT resample). Compute HY cross-correlation at candidate offsets theta in {-30s..+30s, 1s step} on a rolling daily window; lag*_L = argmax |HY(theta)|. Then build the lead-lag-aligned leader signal: take leader L's signed flow / return shifted by lag*_L and feed it as a predictor of EURUSD's next 1m/5m direction. Re-estimate lag*_L per day (it drifts). Restrict the panel to NY session. Pass aligned leader returns + signed flows + the lag* values themselves (regime info) into the cross-pair GBM.
all_candidates.falsifier: HY-recovered lags are unstable day-to-day (|day-over-day lag change| median > 10s = noise) OR the lag-aligned leader signals do not raise purged-OOS EURUSD direction AUC above the fixed-lag lead-lag incumbent -> kill. Pre-register: aligned-signal up-rate of moved bars stays in [.47,.53].
all_candidates.source: Hayashi & Yoshida 2005 (Bernoulli); Huth & Abergel 'High-frequency lead/lag relationships - Empirical facts' (J. Empirical Finance 2014, arXiv 1111.7103); philipperemy/lead-lag library

all_candidates.method: Roll / Corwin-Schultz / Abdi-Ranaldo effective-spread estimators as a transaction-cost-implied liquidity feature and a deriv-faithfulness placebo
all_candidates.what: Three closed-form effective-spread estimators from price-only data: Roll (from negative serial covariance of returns), Corwin-Schultz (from 2-day high-low ranges), Abdi-Ranaldo (from close + high-low). They estimate the bid-ask bounce magnitude. As a feature: spread state conditions when micro signals work. As a PLACEBO: a Roll-MA(1) bid-ask-bounce null verifies that any short-horizon 'edge' is not just monetizing 1s mid-bounce / t,t+1 timing misalignment.
all_candidates.novelty: We have a raw relative-spread column already, but the estimated EFFECTIVE spread (bounce-implied, Roll/CS/AR) is different from quoted spread and is untried. More importantly the Roll-MA(1) microstructure PLACEBO (flagged in our own corpus index as 'untried, high') is a VALIDATION upgrade: a null environment that catches false 1m edges arising from mid-price bounce — directly relevant since 1m single-pair is near-efficient and any apparent signal is bounce-suspect.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1m OHLCV (high/low/close) for CS/AR; 1s mid returns for Roll covariance; existing spread column for cross-check.
all_candidates.input_transform: Roll spread per bar window: s_Roll = 2*sqrt(-cov(dP_t, dP_{t-1})) when cov<0 (from 1s mid returns, rolling). CS spread from rolling 2-bar high-low on 1m OHLCV. AR spread from 1m close + high-low. Use as features: feed the estimated effective-spread series + its ratio to quoted spread (a 'hidden adverse-selection' proxy) to the magnitude model. Use as placebo: build a synthetic mid that adds a Roll-MA(1) bounce of estimated amplitude to a random-walk, run the FULL direction pipeline on it; any 'edge' there is spurious. Subtract that null's accuracy from the real OOS accuracy as a bounce-deflated direction score.
all_candidates.falsifier: Placebo: if the real 1m direction pipeline shows >= the same selective accuracy on the Roll-MA(1) bounce-only synthetic as on real data, the apparent edge is bounce artifact -> the signal is killed (this is a destructive test that PROTECTS the program). Feature: CS/AR/Roll spread adds < +0.003 deflated magnitude AUC over rv+quoted-spread -> drop as feature.

all_candidates.method: Realized semivariance / signed-jump variation imbalance as a SIGN feature (good-vol minus bad-vol) for the cross-pair direction model
all_candidates.what: Split a window's realized variance into upside (RV+) from positive 1s returns and downside (RV-) from negative ones. The signed-jump variation SJ = RV+ - RV- and the semivariance ratio capture whether recent variance was built by up-moves or down-moves; a persistent up-vol dominance is a directional lean distinct from the mean return, and the literature shows negative semivariance has stronger forward effects (asymmetry).

all_candidates.method: Micro-price drift (Stoikov fair-value adjustment) as a 1-step-ahead directional tilt distilled to the bar grid
all_candidates.what: Stoikov's micro-price is a martingale fair value = mid + an imbalance/spread-conditioned adjustment g(imbalance, spread), empirically a better short-horizon predictor than mid or volume-weighted mid. The bar-end micro-price MINUS mid is a small directional tilt (where the fair price sits relative to the quoted mid); a persistent positive tilt predicts the next mid prints higher.
all_candidates.novelty: We have a 'micro' column (simple volume-weighted micro) but NOT the Stoikov ITERATED micro-price (the martingale limit of repeated expected-mid updates, fit by the symmetrized Markov-chain G1/B matrices on (imbalance,spread) states). The fitted-adjustment micro-price is a different, untried estimator; its drift relative to mid, accumulated per bar, is a candidate sign feature at the shortest research horizons (1m).
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick store (mid, imb, spread, micro) EURUSD primarily; extend per-pair from raw tick.
all_candidates.input_transform: Discretize state = (imbalance bucket from imb, spread bucket from spread). Estimate Stoikov G1 (expected next mid-move given state) and transition matrix on TRAIN ticks only; iterate to the micro-price limit M* per bar. Directional tilt tau_t = (M*_t - mid_t)/mid_t. Aggregate tau over each 1m bar (mean and end value), feed tau + sign(tau)-persistence to the 1m direction model. Build cross-pair tau residual for the cross-sectional model. Strictly causal: G1/B matrices frozen from train, applied forward.

all_candidates.method: Marked bivariate Hawkes of POSITIVE vs NEGATIVE jumps -> time-varying conditional skewness as a SIGN feature
all_candidates.what: Fit a 2-type marked Hawkes where the two event streams are signed price jumps (up-jumps, down-jumps), each with a self- and CROSS-excitation kernel and a mark (jump-size) distribution. The asymmetry of the branching matrix (alpha_up<-down vs alpha_down<-up) makes the conditional distribution time-varying-SKEWED: when up-jumps preferentially trigger more up-jumps than down-jumps trigger down-jumps, the forward return distribution is right-skewed -> positive expected sign. The predictive quantity is the model-implied next-horizon E[sign] = (integrated up-intensity*E[mark+] - integrated down-intensity*E[mark-]) over t..t+H, NOT the raw intensity count.
all_candidates.novelty: Already-tried Hawkes used UP-TICK vs DOWN-TICK ARRIVAL counts -> lambda_up-lambda_down, which is provably sign-INVARIANT (counts, not signed magnitudes) and decayed before 120s. This is different on two axes: (1) events are SIZE-thresholded signed JUMPS (Lee-Mykland filtered), not every tick; (2) the predictor is the marked, cross-excitation-driven conditional SKEW (signed first moment of the compensated marked intensity), a genuine direction mechanism. Cross-excitation between + and - jumps is never in the kill-list.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1s tick mid (EURUSD features_tick) and/or 1m close per pair; bar 'close' + rv_12/rv_24 from the 239-feat store for the local-vol jump threshold.
all_candidates.input_transform: From 1s tick mid (or 1m close), run a Lee-Mykland test: r_i / (local bipower-vol estimate) > c => jump; sign(r_i) labels it up-jump or down-jump; |r_i| is the mark. This yields two marked event streams (timestamps + marks). Fit with tick.hawkes (HawkesExpKern, 2-dim, exp kernel) or a marked extension; estimate the 2x2 branching matrix + mark-conditional-intensity. At each bar t, compute the H-ahead expected signed compensator E[N_up*mbar_up - N_down*mbar_down | F_t] as ONE scalar direction feature fed to the m5xp/m15 GBM (so it competes inside the certified cross-pair ensemble, sign-invariance-checked).

all_candidates.method: Multivariate cross-pair Hawkes EXCITATION MATRIX (ADM4) as a directed lead-lag network -> cross-sectional direction
all_candidates.what: Fit a 7-dimensional Hawkes on the signed-jump streams of all 7 USD pairs simultaneously. The off-diagonal branching coefficients alpha_{ij} are a DIRECTED, causal excitation graph: alpha_{EURUSD<-GBPUSD} > 0 means a GBPUSD jump raises EURUSD's near-term jump intensity. Use the row of the excitation matrix to form, for each target pair at time t, a 'borrowed intensity' = sum_j alpha_{target<-j} * recent-signed-activity_j, i.e. an excitation-weighted cross-pair momentum that predicts the SIGN of the next target move.
all_candidates.novelty: Cross-pair direction so far = USD-residual / OFI common-factor / lead-lag-residual / transfer-entropy gate / IPCA — all CORRELATION- or regression-based on returns. A Hawkes excitation matrix is a fundamentally different estimand: directed CONDITIONAL-INTENSITY causality on the EVENT (jump) timing, asymmetric by construction (alpha_ij != alpha_ji), capturing WHO-EXCITES-WHOM at the jump level rather than contemporaneous return covariance. ADM4 (low-rank+sparse) cross-pair Hawkes is not in the tried list.
all_candidates.required_inputs: cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (5.3M rows, all 7 USD pairs) and/or per-pair 1m close; rv from 239-feat for thresholding.
all_candidates.input_transform: For each of 7 pairs derive a signed-jump event stream (Lee-Mykland on 1m or 5m returns; sign = direction). Align all 7 onto a common clock. Per target pair, feature = sum_j Phi[target,j] * exp-decayed recent signed jump load of pair j (a forward excitation forecast). Add this single cross-pair-excitation scalar to the certified cross-sectional ensemble; CPCV with 1-horizon purge/embargo. Concentrate eval on NY session (where the certified cross-sectional edge lives).

all_candidates.novelty: We have many gates (bb_width compression x session, microstructure-quality, vol regime) but NONE based on the self-excitation / endogeneity of the point process. Branching ratio is a single interpretable scalar measuring market reflexivity/criticality that is orthogonal to volatility level (a calm market can be highly endogenous and vice-versa). Never in the tried list. Recent work resolves the subcritical-vs-critical paradox, making the estimate trustworthy.

all_candidates.method: ACD / price-DURATION as a MAGNITUDE predictor (duration-based volatility, jump-robust)

all_candidates.method: Hawkes time-rescaling RESIDUALS as a leakage-aware regime/validation diagnostic + representation
all_candidates.what: After fitting any Hawkes to a pair's event stream, the time-rescaling theorem says the compensator-transformed inter-event times xi_k = integral of lambda over [t_{k-1},t_k] are iid Exp(1) IFF the model is correct. Deviations (KS distance, ACF of xi, local over/under-dispersion) localize WHERE the point-process model breaks — i.e. where dynamics are anomalous/regime-shifting. Use the rolling residual-dispersion as (a) a VALIDATION instrument to detect regime change / structural break in the event dynamics, and (b) a representation feature (local 'surprise' = how much current activity exceeds the self-excited expectation) feeding the gate.
all_candidates.novelty: Our validation arsenal is CPCV/deflated-Sharpe/PBO (overfit control on the LABEL side); time-rescaling residuals test the INPUT generative model and flag nonstationary regime onsets in event timing — a different, point-process-native diagnostic never used here. As a feature, 'excess intensity vs self-excited expectation' is distinct from raw intensity (it is the standardized surprise/innovation of the point process).
all_candidates.required_inputs: any fitted Hawkes from the candidates above; per-pair event streams; existing regime/gate machinery.
all_candidates.input_transform: Fit the univariate (or cross-pair) Hawkes; compute compensator residuals xi_k. all_candidates.method: Hawkes ONE-FACTOR cojump model: systemic vs idiosyncratic decomposition for cross-sectional direction
all_candidates.what: Postulate an unobservable market-factor jump point process; when it fires, each USD pair jumps with pair-specific probability p_i; each pair also has an idiosyncratic Hawkes. Calibrate to separate SYSTEMIC (USD-wide) jumps from IDIOSYNCRATIC ones. The cross-sectional direction edge is the conditional sign AFTER removing the systemic component: an idiosyncratic jump in one pair, in the absence of a systemic jump, is more likely to mean-revert or to lead a specific peer — sharpening the residual cross-sectional signal beyond the linear USD-factor we already strip.
all_candidates.novelty: We strip a USD COMMON FACTOR linearly (USD-residual). The Hawkes factor model strips the common JUMP factor at the EVENT level and gives a probabilistic systemic-vs-idiosyncratic LABEL per jump, which the linear residual cannot (it cannot tell a 1-pair idiosyncratic move from a partial systemic one). Conditioning the cross-sectional sign on 'idiosyncratic-only jump' is a new decomposition not in the tried list.

all_candidates.input_transform: Detect jumps per pair (Lee-Mykland on 1m/5m). Build the cojump count process (how many pairs jump in the same bar). Fit the Bormetti-Lillo Hawkes one-factor model (market-factor Hawkes + per-pair idiosyncratic Hawkes; calibrate p_i via the cojump-count distribution + a Hawkes fit to the factor). At each bar, classify the target's recent jump as systemic-prob vs idiosyncratic-prob; feature = idiosyncratic-conditioned signed load. Gate/feed the cross-sectional direction ensemble; CPCV in NY session.

all_candidates.method: FourierGNN hypervariate graph + Fourier Graph Operator (FGO)
all_candidates.what: Treat EVERY (pair, timestamp) scalar in a sliding window as a single graph node, build one space-time fully-connected 'hypervariate' graph, and do message passing as complex matrix multiplication in the Fourier (frequency) domain via the FGO. Spatial (cross-pair) and temporal dependencies are modeled jointly in one operator instead of stacked GCN+RNN, and FGO is provably equivalent to a time-domain graph convolution but at log-linear cost.
all_candidates.novelty: Our cataloged GNNs (RSR/TGC, FinGAT, THGNN, MDGNN, Multi-GCGRU, DeltaLag) all use pair=node + a separate temporal encoder (LSTM/GRU/transformer/cross-attention). FourierGNN's node = a single (pair,time) value and its message passing happens in frequency space; this is a categorically different graph construction never tried here. It is also the engineered-feature, frequency-domain alternative to the Chronos-2 group-attention that already FAILED to recover the cross-sectional edge.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (5.3M rows, 7 USD pairs); 239-feat store optional as extra node channels.
all_candidates.input_transform: Resample the 7-pair panel to the target horizon (5m/15m/30m bars). For each bar t, form a window of the last L bars (e.g. L=32) of a stationary signal per pair: log-return r=diff(log(close)) z-scored per pair per session. Stack into a tensor [7 pairs x L x C] where C are channels {return, rv_12, ofi_proxy, dist_to_high}. Flatten to N=7*L*C hypervariate nodes; embed each scalar node to d=64 with a shared linear layer + learned (pair,time) positional embedding. Run 2-3 stacked FGOs (rfft over the time axis -> complex linear mixing -> irfft), readout ONLY the EURUSD-at-time-t nodes, sigmoid head -> P(up). Label = sign(wc_ret over +1s-lagged mid-to-mid). all_candidates.method: Shift-invariant top-AND-bottom listwise loss (generalized ListMLE / generalized Plackett-Luce)
all_candidates.what: A listwise learn-to-rank surrogate loss that simultaneously emphasizes the TOP and BOTTOM of the cross-sectional rank list (motivated by long-short), is endogenously shift-invariant (symmetric), generalizes ListMLE, and under different transformation functions becomes consistent with binary-classification 0-1 loss. One coherent scoring function ranks all 7 pairs per bar; you trade the top (up) and bottom (down) of the ranked list.
all_candidates.novelty: Our cross-pair work used MSE/cross-entropy and (cataloged-but-untried) RSR PAIRWISE max-margin ranking; this is a LISTWISE loss explicitly engineered to rescue the BOTTOM (the dead DOWN side) with a single coherent ranker, avoiding the 'two models contradict / buy+sell same asset' failure of side-split specialists we already killed. Shift-invariance also removes the per-bar market-wide drift that pollutes single-pair direction.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (7 pairs); the 239-feat store as per-pair per-bar feature vectors.
all_candidates.input_transform: At each horizon bar t, build a cross-section: 7 rows (one per USD pair), each a feature vector x_{i,t} from the 239-feat store (returns, rv_12/24, atr, bb_width, rangepos, session flags) PLUS USD-common-factor / USD-residual features. Rank label y_{i,t} = ordinal rank of each pair's forward signed wc_ret at bar t (1..7). Train a shared scoring net f(x)->scalar with the shift-invariant listwise loss over the 7-pair list per bar; sign-normalize all 7 to USD direction first so 'up' is comparable across pairs (invert JPY/CHF/CAD legs). At inference, EURUSD's UP signal = it lands in top-k of the ranked list; DOWN = bottom-k. Purge+embargo=1 horizon.
all_candidates.falsifier: Kill if, on purged OOS, neither the top-k (UP) nor bottom-k (DOWN) selected EURUSD bars clear 0.541 win-rate, OR if the listwise loss does not beat the same net trained with plain BCE on the identical cross-section (loss is inert). Specifically the DOWN side must reach >=0.541 on >=1 horizon, else the 'rescue the bottom' claim is falsified.
all_candidates.source: Constructing long-short stock portfolio with a new listwise learn-to-rank algorithm (Zhang, Wu, Chen 2021, arXiv:2104.12484); also Building Cross-Sectional Systematic Strategies By Learning to Rank (arXiv:2012.07149)

all_candidates.method: Currency-as-node / FX-rate-as-edge triangular no-arbitrage graph GNN (edge-level prediction)
all_candidates.what: Instead of pair=node, model the 8 currencies (USD,EUR,GBP,AUD,NZD,JPY,CHF,CAD) as NODES and each tradable rate as a directed EDGE. Forecasting becomes edge-level regression/classification on a multi-currency graph; message passing propagates information through shared-currency hubs and is naturally constrained by triangular no-arbitrage (EUR->USD->JPY vs EUR->JPY). Currency node embeddings absorb the common USD factor endogenously.
all_candidates.novelty: Every cataloged graph method (and our own cross-pair features) uses pair=node with a correlation/lead-lag adjacency. Putting CURRENCIES as nodes and RATES as edges is a structurally different graph that bakes in the triangular constraint and gives a principled, learned USD-common-factor (the USD node embedding) rather than an engineered residual. Directly targets the certified-edge mechanism (USD-common-factor / USD-residual) with a graph that respects FX topology.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Cross-pair aligned 1-min panel (7 USD pairs give 7 of the edges incident to the USD node; crosses like EURJPY are derivable by triangulation from USD legs).
all_candidates.input_transform: Nodes = 8 currencies. Edges = the 7 on-disk USD pairs (USD<->X) plus synthesized crosses (EURJPY = EURUSD*USDJPY etc.) so the graph is richer than a star. Edge feature at bar t = stationary signal of that rate: log-return over the horizon, rv_12, atr, ofi_proxy, all z-scored. Node features initialized to a learned currency embedding. Run 2-3 message-passing layers (edge->node aggregation then node->edge readout, e.g. a relational GCN or EGNN). Read out the EURUSD edge -> P(up) head. Add a no-arbitrage consistency penalty: sum over triangles of (logEURUSD+logUSDJPY-logEURJPY)^2 as an auxiliary loss to regularize. Label as deriv-faithful wc_ret sign.
all_candidates.falsifier: Kill if the USD-node embedding learned by the graph does not reproduce/beat the hand-engineered USD-common-factor (compare OOS AUC of EURUSD-edge readout vs the certified USD-residual book), or if the triangular auxiliary loss provides no lift over the same GNN without it. Build hyperedges for genuine higher-order FX structures (a currency-triangle EURUSD-USDJPY-EURJPY; a 'USD-strength basket' hyperedge over all 7 USD pairs; lead-lag clusters) and run hypergraph convolution so a group of co-moving pairs jointly informs EURUSD's direction.

Higher-order GROUP relations (a whole triangle or the whole USD basket as one unit) have never been modeled here. This captures 'when the entire USD complex moves together' as a single hyperedge signal, which pairwise correlation features dilute.

all_candidates.method: Probabilistic graph-structure learning (GTS / NRI) for a sparse stochastic cross-pair adjacency
all_candidates.what: Rather than fixing the cross-pair graph to a correlation/lead-lag matrix, LEARN the adjacency end-to-end as a sparse stochastic graph: GTS learns one global probabilistic structure over the 7 series via a parameterized Bernoulli/Gumbel-softmax adjacency; NRI uses an encoder to infer a DIFFERENT latent interaction graph per window. The inferred edges and their uncertainty become the message-passing structure for direction.

Discrete, SPARSE, probabilistic structure learning with a reparameterized Bernoulli adjacency (and per-window structures via NRI) is untried; it can discover non-obvious, regime-specific cross-pair links and yields edge-uncertainty usable as a confidence GATE.

Use the edge POSTERIOR PROBABILITY incident to EURUSD as a confidence gate: trade only bars where EURUSD has a high-probability incoming edge. Purge+embargo=1 horizon; learn A only on train groups.

all_candidates.method: TENOR — joint estimation of a TIME-VARYING label-noise function T(t) with the classifier (Learning under Temporal Label Noise)
all_candidates.what: Our binary sign label is noisy AND the noise rate is non-stationary (efficient in Asia/London, less so in NY; quiet vs trending regimes). TENOR parameterizes a small neural noise function T(t) = P(observed sign | true sign, time/regime features) and trains it jointly with the direction classifier via a forward-corrected loss, so the model recovers the CLEAN posterior P(true up | x) instead of fitting the time-varying corruption. This is a principled, learned analogue of the repo's hand-built NY-session gate.
all_candidates.novelty: Repo killed only STATIC label smoothing and static relabeling. TENOR's noise process is explicitly time/regime-VARYING (the killed-set has no time-varying noise-transition model). It is also distinct from meta-labeling (which gates a fixed primary) — TENOR corrects the loss that TRAINS the primary, recovering clean sign where the corruption is heaviest off-NY.
all_candidates.required_inputs: 1m OHLCV 239-feat store (features) + cross-pair panel; per-bar time-of-day + DST-correct session id from sessions.py; forward sign label from harness/contig_fwd at H=5m/10m.
all_candidates.input_transform: Label y_i = sign(wc_ret) at horizon H (ties=loss kept as observed). Build a per-bar 'time context' vector t_i = [sin/cos minute-of-day, session_id(NY/LDN/Asia), rv_24, bb_width-percentile]. Noise function T_phi(t_i) is a 2-layer MLP -> 2x2 row-stochastic matrix (softmax rows). Classifier f_theta(x_i) on the 239 features (cross-pair augmented). Loss = CE(observed y_i, T_phi(t_i) @ softmax(f_theta(x_i))) (forward correction). Warm-start T toward identity, anneal a volume-min-entropy prior on T so it does not collapse. Deploy: use f_theta directly (clean head); gate with existing ACI. Eval under refit-CPCV at the NY operating point — falsifier-protected.
all_candidates.falsifier: Under per-fold refit-CPCV (8 groups, k=2, purge+embargo=1H), the TENOR clean head's NY-session win-rate p10 does NOT exceed the certified cross-pair book's p10 (5m .596 / 10m .605) by >=0.5pp on the binding 2025 year; OR T_phi collapses to identity (no time-varying noise found) => KILL. Up-rate of taken bars must stay in [.47,.53].
all_candidates.source: Learning under Temporal Label Noise (TENOR), arXiv:2402.04398 (2024)

all_candidates.method: Meta Label Correction (MLC) — bi-level learnable label-CORRECTOR network (not a gate)
all_candidates.what: A meta-model (label-correction net) emits soft corrected labels y'_i for each bar; the direction model is trained on y'; both are co-optimized via bi-level optimization so the corrected labels are exactly those that minimize VALIDATION loss. Where the raw 50/50 sign is pure noise, MLC learns to soften/flip it toward the regime-consistent value, concentrating signal where it exists.
all_candidates.novelty: Repo's relabeling (triple-barrier relabel) and label smoothing are FIXED transforms applied before training. MLC's correction is LEARNED end-to-end against held-out performance via bi-level optimization — a fundamentally different mechanism (the labels themselves are trainable parameters tied to OOS loss), never tried. Distinct from meta-LABELING (which leaves labels intact and gates predictions).
all_candidates.required_inputs: 239-feat store + cross-pair features; forward sign labels at 5m/10m; a small meta-feature set for the corrector (rv, session, |wc_ret| decile, primary logit).
all_candidates.input_transform: Lower level: GBM-or-MLP primary g_theta(x) on 239 cross-pair feats. Upper level: corrector h_alpha(meta_i) -> soft label y'_i in [0,1], meta_i = [raw y_i, |wc_ret| decile, rv_24, session_id, g_theta logit]. Inner: theta* = argmin CE(g_theta(x), y'). Outer: alpha = argmin CE(g_{theta*}(x_val), y_val) on a PURGED held-out fold (purge=1H to avoid leakage from overlapping labels). Use first-order/T1-approx (EBOMLC trick) so it runs on CPU/8GB. Inspect learned corrections: they should up-weight large-|ret| bars (where sign is predictable) and soften tiny moves.
all_candidates.falsifier: On refit-CPCV, the MLC-trained primary's p10 does not beat the BCE primary by >=0.5pp at the NY operating point; OR the learned corrector reduces to identity / pure |ret|-weighting (which the repo already tested as magweight and found regime-fragile) => KILL. Must clear breakeven 0.541 on purged OOS.

all_candidates.method: Two-Level Uncertainty cross-sectional RANK meta-labeling ('When Alpha Breaks')
all_candidates.what: Our ONLY certified direction edge is cross-sectional across 7 USD pairs in NY. This method trains a secondary model g(x) that predicts the PRIMARY ranker's expected rank-displacement / error per pair-bar, then trades only the top/bottom decile pairs whose predicted rank is confident. It is meta-labeling specialized to a cross-sectional ranking primary rather than a single-asset binary primary.
all_candidates.novelty: Repo's meta-labeling was applied to a single-pair primary on 'orthogonal axes' and collapsed under refit-CPCV. This is meta-labeling on the CROSS-SECTIONAL ranker (the edge that DID certify), predicting per-pair rank-error to choose WHICH pairs to act on each NY bar — a target the repo never gave a secondary model. Directly attacks the certified edge's worst-regime p10, not a dead single-pair channel.

Secondary target = was the primary's top/bottom-decile pick PROFITABLE (deriv-faithful, ties lose). Train secondary on purged OOF primary preds. all_candidates.method: Trend-scanning labels with t-value-as-sample-weight (López de Prado, regression variant)
all_candidates.what: Instead of a fixed-H sign label, fit OLS close~time over a window of forward look-aheads L in {2..H_max}, pick L* maximizing |t-value| of the slope, label = sign(slope at L*), and SAMPLE-WEIGHT each bar by |t-value|. This adapts the label horizon per bar and concentrates training on bars whose forward trend is statistically real, discarding the in-between noise that floods the fixed-H sign.

The mechanism differs: trend-scanning picks the most-significant horizon PER BAR (variable label horizon) and the t-value weighting is a genuinely different sample weight than the killed |ret|-weight (it weights STATISTICAL trend strength, not move size). The 2024 MQL5/RF result used t-values as meta-label sample weights specifically.

CRITICAL leakage guard: trend-scanning looks FORWARD so the embargo for CPCV must equal H_max (not H) — purge+embargo=H_max bars. Train GBM on cross-pair feats with sample_weight=w_i; eval the SIGN at the deriv horizon (re-map label back to the tradeable 5m/10m settlement for scoring, since trend-scan H* != settlement H). Compare to fixed-H sign baseline.

all_candidates.what: Dynamically choose each bar's label horizon by scanning 5 time resolutions and keeping only horizons where a Granger-causality / transfer-entropy test confirms the chosen predictor->future-return link is CAUSAL (not spurious), then MAML-adapt the labeler. Distinct from CCM (which tested coupling of OFI->return, killed) — here TE filters the label's own horizon.

all_candidates.method: Sequential-bootstrap sample-uniqueness as a VALIDATION / deflation refinement (not as a signal lever)
all_candidates.what: Compute average-uniqueness u_i = mean(1/concurrency) over each label's lifespan from the fixed forward horizon, then (a) set CPCV embargo and effective-sample-size from realized uniqueness rather than a flat 1-horizon embargo, and (b) deflate the Sharpe / PBO using the uniqueness-corrected number of INDEPENDENT bars. This tightens the certification math itself, where the repo's edges live or die on p10.
all_candidates.novelty: Repo catalogs sample-uniqueness as a BACKLOG SIGNAL lever ('tighter CI, not new signal', never run). The novel framing is to use it on the VALIDATION side: the cross-pair edge is certified/killed by CPCV p10 with a FLAT embargo; replacing flat embargo with realized per-bar uniqueness can change the deflated number and the path-clear fraction. This is a validation-target use, not a training-weight use.
all_candidates.required_inputs: Forward label horizon (5m/10m bars) for concurrency; existing per-result JSONs and CPCV harness; no new data.
all_candidates.input_transform: For each bar build the label-span interval [t_i, t_i+H]; concurrency c_t = #intervals covering t; uniqueness of bar i = mean over its span of 1/c_t. (1) Replace the flat embargo in cpcv with a data-driven embargo = horizon where cross-label concurrency decays below 1.1 (often < H for trending bars, > H for choppy). all_candidates.method: Parity Calibration (direction-of-change recalibration of a magnitude/quantile model)
all_candidates.what: Chung et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.18655): given a probabilistic regression forecast of the next value, the probability the value INCREASES is exactly the predictive-CDF evaluated at the current value, 1 - F_t(y_{t-1}). They then ONLINE-recalibrate that single binary 'parity' probability with a 1-D recalibrator (online Platt / temperature) — turning a calibrated *magnitude* forecaster into a calibrated *direction* probability for free, beating naive direction classifiers on weather/electricity.

Parity calibration is the missing bridge: derive P(up) = 1 - F(0) from the magnitude/quantile predictive distribution we ALREADY certified (30m magAUC .744, 5m/10m strong), then online-recalibrate that derived sign-probability. This is NOT the ACI gate (which gates a fixed meta-score), NOT triple-barrier, NOT a new direction model — it extracts a direction signal from the magnitude distribution, which the sign-invariance theorem says is the forecastable object. Untried entirely.

ranked.method: Lead-lag signature transform (Hoff staircase -> depth-2/3 log-signature CROSS-TERMS) on the 7-pair panel into the cross-sectional GBM

Randomized signatures sidestep this with a frozen random controlled-ODE recursion giving a ~256-d state that provably approximates the full signature — feasible at depth>2 on 8 channels for the first time. It is the path-space analogue of the ESN/GRU reservoir we KILLED but with a different (iterated-integral, reparametrization-invariant) inductive bias, so it is a genuine retest of 'is there path-geometry the reservoir's generic recurrence missed'. Pure numpy/torch, no special lib, <1s/window batched.
