HAVOK's SVD of a delay-Hankel matrix yields a near-linear system whose LAST low-energy coordinate v_r is an intermittent, SIGNED forcing that spikes BEFORE bursts/large excursions — a dynamic precursor with sign, unlike permutation entropy (static, null) or rv (sign-blind). On the cross-pair state it could lead regime-changing moves. Pure numpy SVD, streaming/windowed, CPU-cheap.

Extract |v_r| energy over next horizon (gate) and sign(v_r * leading-loading) (direction bias).

ranked.why_promising: Operator-spectral change-point detection gates on the SYSTEM's effective dynamics/spectrum changing — a fundamentally different signal than rv or bb_width (the gate we already use). A documented streaming impl (odmd-subid-cpd) makes it laptop-cheap and causal. Transitions are exactly where a frozen direction book fails and where mean-reversion flips to trend; also predicts large |move| (magnitude cross-use).

Per step: residual_t=||x_{t+1}-A_hat x_t||, spectral_radius_t=max|eig(A_hat)|; z-score both -> 'regime_stable' / 'transition' flags.

ranked.method: FASCL — Future-Aligned Soft Contrastive Learning on the 7-pair panel (target-supervised cross-sectional embedding) -> GBM
ranked.why_promising: Every learned rep we ran (Kronos decode_s1, Chronos-2) is SIGN-BLIND (positives from augmentation/reconstruction), so the geometry never sees the forward return — the exact failure mode. FASCL makes the soft contrastive target the FUTURE forward-return correlation between pairs; its ablation shows the observation-aligned variant (=what TS2Vec/Kronos effectively do) loses ~3.3%. It directly supervises the embedding with the cross-sectional co-movement that IS our certified edge — a mechanism with 0 contrastive impls in the repo. Higher effort (train an encoder) but aimed squarely at the hardest/most-valuable gap with a clear reason prior reps failed.
ranked.input_transform: From panel_<year>.parquet: per-(pair,bar) windows L=64-128 of log-returns + rv/rangepos/atr (RevIN per window). # COMPLETENESS CRITIC — Critique of the 110-candidate slate

I verified the repo and corpus directly (Tier 1) before writing. Key ground-truth checks: `m30_sig.py` (only truncated level-2 Lévy area, single-instrument price/OFI — so signature *kernels* and cross-pair signatures are genuinely untried); `grep fracdiff *.py` → **zero hits** (fractional differencing has never been run here despite the memory note calling it "cataloged"); corpus index has **0** entries for signature/koopman/dmd/wavelet-scattering/persistent-homology/fracdiff/mamba/deltanet/sundial/quarticity; `min1_hurst.py` + `m5_signinv_dir.py` (variance-ratio/Hurst already run, standalone + incremental); and most importantly `MAGNITUDE_FINDINGS.md §6f` — **the time-of-day/deseasonalized-RV "win" was RETRACTED 2026-06-07: it fails forward (2026 ΔAUC −0.054) and is KILLED for deployment.** That last fact breaks the stated falsifier of multiple candidates and is the most consequential thing in this review.

## A. The 0.758 magnitude baseline is a phantom — fix the falsifiers before any magnitude work

The prompt and at least six magnitude candidates (Log-NCDE, SCINet, MOMENT-MSE, expected-signature, WSS, MFDFA Δα, HARQ, Wasserstein-of-diagrams) pre-register against "the rv+time-of-day baseline, 30m AUC 0.758." Per `MAGNITUDE_FINDINGS.md §6f` (verified verbatim this session) that 0.758 **does not exist as a deployable baseline** — `+tod` gave +0.0140 pooled-CPCV but `deseason_fwd.py` shows 2024 +.020 → 2025 −.009 → 2026 −.054, "materially WORSE (.683 vs .737)," explicitly **"KILLED for deployment."** The durable lesson recorded there: *pooled CPCV does not catch non-stationary-feature memorization.* Consequence for the slate: every magnitude candidate whose entire value proposition is "learn intraday seasonality better than hand clock dummies" (CoST seasonal head, TabPFN-TS calendar covariates, the seasonal half of WSS, T-JEPA-if-it-just-restates-ToD) is **attacking a target that was already shown to be a forward-decaying mirage.** These should either be killed pre-emptively or have their falsifier rewritten to: *beat the forward-robust BASE rv30/rv120 model (.74–.79 every year) on a frozen-past per-year holdout, not pooled CPCV.* The slate's authors did not know §6f; it post-dates most of their reasoning. This is the highest-priority correction in the whole review.

## B. Methodology families entirely ABSENT from all 17 clusters

These are real gaps, not nitpicks — nothing in the 110 touches them:

1. **GARCH/HAR econometric volatility models as the magnitude backbone.** The slate has HARQ (one realized-quarticity correction) but **no GARCH-family** at all: no EGARCH/GJR (leverage asymmetry), no realized-GARCH, no HAR-RV-J (jump component), no **Markov-switching multifractal (MSM)**. This is the single largest omission given that magnitude is the program's *only* robust edge. The corpus confirms it (`grep -i garch` context shows only one DL-GARCH hybrid). FX realized vol is the most-studied object in econometrics and the slate skips the canonical models in favor of TDA/signature exotica. HAR-RV-J in particular decomposes RV into continuous + jump parts — orthogonal to rv30/rv120 and forward-robust by construction (it's a within-window decomposition, not a calendar memorization).

2. **Has/Realized-semivariance & signed-jump direction.** `MAGNITUDE_FINDINGS.md` itself flags "semivariance RV" as a queued idea. Realized **semivariance** (RS⁺ vs RS⁻, Barndorff-Nielsen) splits upside vs downside realized variance — and the RS⁺−RS⁻ *signed* component is one of the few volatility constructs with documented *directional* predictive content (Patton-Sheppard "Good Volatility, Bad Volatility"). The slate has nothing here despite it being directly on-disk-computable from 1s ticks and theoretically matched to the dead DOWN side. This is a notable miss for **direction**, not just magnitude.

3. **Hawkes / self-exciting point processes on the tick stream.** The 1s tick + trade-count store is ideal for a marked Hawkes process; the **branching ratio** and **excitation kernel decay** are forward-robust intensity/clustering features that lead large moves. Zero candidates. The closest (Mamba-dt activity clock) is a crude proxy. Hawkes is the textbook model for the exact "event-time / liquidity clock" the slate gropes at via SSM dt-injection.

4. **Change-point / regime econometrics outside Koopman.** The slate's regime detection is all dynamical-systems exotica (CROCKER, DMD-residual, HAVOK). Missing: **Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCPD)**, **HMM/HSMM with duration**, and **binary-segmentation / PELT** on the cross-pair correlation series. BOCPD in particular gives a calibrated run-length posterior that is a principled gate — far cheaper and better-understood than a CROCKER tensor, and it directly attacks the corr(VAL,OOS)=−0.54 non-stationarity trap.

5. **Quantile / distributional DIRECTION via expectiles or quantile-crossing.** TimesFM-quantile and Lag-Llama-CDF appear, but no **direct quantile-regression forest / LightGBM-quantile** producing P(ret>0) from the existing 239 features — the cheapest possible probabilistic-direction baseline, and a necessary control before any TSFM quantile claim is credible. Its absence means the TSFM quantile candidates have no fair ablation partner.

6. **Causal-inference / instrumental structure for lead-lag.** Lead-lag is treated purely associatively (signatures, DMD phase, transfer entropy). No **PCMCI / Granger-with-FDR / structural VAR with sign restrictions** to isolate *which* pair causally leads under the USD factor. Given that the certified edge IS cross-pair lead-lag, a causal-discovery method that prunes spurious contemporaneous correlation is arguably more on-target than any signature variant.

## C. Input transforms nobody proposed (the user explicitly emphasized this)

The slate's transform cluster is wavelet/SSA/VMD/fracdiff-heavy but misses several with strong priors:

1. **Fractional differencing is mis-catalogued as "tried."** The FFD candidate exists, but my grep proves **fracdiff has never been implemented in this repo** — so it is not "composing a known transform with cross-pair," it is introducing the transform for the first time. This raises its value: the certified cross-pair edge is built entirely on integer-differenced returns (`crosspair.py` appends peer return/rv columns), which destroy the long-memory level co-movement where a slow USD trend lives. FFD-then-residualize is the highest-priority *transform* idea and it is under-rated at "ev: medium."

2. **No tick-imbalance / dollar / volume bars (Lopez de Prado information-driven bars).** Everything is sampled in **clock time** (1m bars). Information-driven bars (sample a bar every N ticks / $X traded / fixed imbalance) are *the* canonical fix for the non-IID, heteroskedastic sampling that makes clock-time FX returns near-unpredictable, and they synchronize the 7 pairs on *information* rather than wall-clock — potentially sharpening the cross-sectional alignment far more than any model. The slate gestures at "event time" only inside a Mamba dt-parameter (a deep-net proxy); the clean econometric version (rebar the raw data) is absent and is plausibly the single most impactful input reshaping available.

3. **No intraday seasonal *adjustment of returns themselves* (only of vol).** The deseasonalization work standardized RV; nobody proposed dividing returns by the seasonal vol profile (a "vol-time" clock / subordination) so that the direction model sees vol-standardized increments — a different and forward-safer use of seasonality than adding calendar dummies (which §6f killed).

4. **No cross-pair whitening / Mahalanobis residualization.** USD-residual is computed by factor regression; nobody proposed **ZCA/Cholesky whitening** of the 7-pair covariance so the residual channels are statistically independent before the GBM — a standard preconditioning that can expose lead-lag the factor regression smears.

5. **No phase/Hilbert-envelope or instantaneous-frequency transform** of the cross-pair factor (distinct from VMD's per-mode IF) — the analytic-signal phase of the USD common factor is a natural cyclicity coordinate untouched by the slate.

## D. False-novelty flags (candidates that are secretly duplicates)

- **Variance-ratio/Hurst/roughness-index candidates as DIRECTION/gate (Cont-Das roughness, NVAR-ridge-standalone, MFDFA-for-direction).** `m5_signinv_dir.py` already ran rolling Hurst (variance-of-sums AND R/S) and the broader sign-invariant complexity family *both standalone for true sign and incremental into the m5xp cross-pair set*, with a pre-registered KILL that fired. The program's **sign-invariance theorem** says these gate SIZE not SIGN. So any new candidate claiming a *direction* edge from a roughness/Hurst/persistence scalar is re-running a killed experiment under a new name. They remain legitimate only as **magnitude** features — and there, MFDFA Δα/c2 must clear the "redundant-with-rv |corr|>0.9" bar the candidate itself names, which is a high hurdle given rv30/rv120 already capture vol level.
